perspective:
Jose Castillo has access to the following information:

- He works with Patricia Ndiaye at a community bank, where he occasionally helps with maintenance and repairs.
- He has observed that Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual during recent shifts, which stood out because she is usually vibrant.
- He asked Patricia if she was okay, and she told him it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked him for asking.
- He offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk, and she said she appreciated that and that it meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He brought up financial planning and offered to discuss budgeting tips; Patricia said she was overwhelmed with bills and would take him up on the offer soon.
- After that, he worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances, and he told Patricia he wanted to help, not pry.
- Patricia assured him she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful he offered to help.
- He told Patricia he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend; she said she appreciated that and felt good knowing she had someone to turn to.
- He later asked Patricia about weekend plans; she said she was fine and planned a quiet weekend at home. He offered again to be there if she needed anything, and she thanked him.
- He has continued to check in with Patricia at work; she has said she’s busy but handling it, thanked him for checking in, and said it was great to have his support.
- He has maintained a supportive presence and offered help, including small things like grabbing coffee.
final_response:
Yes. After I reassured Patricia that I respected her privacy and just wanted to support her as a friend, I continued checking in on her and offering small forms of help, like grabbing coffee. So my intention shifted from backing off while staying supportive to continuing to be supportive.

ANSWER: b
